newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Oil price may rise later this year - Kuwait's Mazeed.
newsitem.headline: Oil price may rise later this year - Kuwait's Mazeed.

text.p: Kuwait Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi predicted a rise in world oil prices due to low winter stocks, the Kuwait News Agency (KUNA) reported on Tuesday.

"Crude prices naturally rise during the winter (in the northern hemisphere) and the period prior to that when oil reserves (stockpiles) by many states, especially the consuming industrial nations, reaches low levels," the minister told KUNA in an interview in Bahrain.
"Oil prices will rise according to these indicators," he added without giving any estimates.
Oil prices have dropped by some 30 percent in recent months, currently trading below $18 a barrel.

When asked about Kuwait's longstading demand for a higher OPEC quota, Mazeedi said "We would like to maintain these prices," adding that OPEC ministers would discuss in June "all matters related to crude, quantities and prices".

On Saturday Mazeedi told parliament "Production, in accordance with (OPEC) ceiling, will be increased from (Kuwait's current quota of) two million (bpd) to 2.4 million in the year 2000 and to three million (afterwards)."

The tiny Gulf Arab state, which controls about 10 percent of the world's proven crude reserves, has a current production capacity of 2.5 million bpd which it plans to increase to three million bpd early in the next century.
Mazeedi told KUNA that the government's programme over the next four years calls for the drilling of some 649 new oil wells.
